## Table S1. Major sudden stratospheric warmings, 1985/86–2024/25

Major SSWs identified from the first reversal of the daily-mean zonal-mean zonal wind at 60°N and 10 hPa in ERA5, with at least 20 consecutive westerly days between events and final warmings excluded unless westerlies return for at least 10 consecutive days before 30 April (Charlton and Polvani 2007). All events up to 2023 coincide exactly (zero-day offset) with the ERA5 central dates of the NOAA SSW Compendium (Butler et al. 2017); the two events of 2024 postdate that reference list.

## Table S2. Termination hazard model: primary predictor family

39 causal predictors, measured on day k or earlier (station Tmin and Tmax of day k; ERA5 at 00 UTC of day k; RRWP R lagged by 7 days or trailing envelopes), adjusted for log event age, day of the season, the same-day national Tmin anomaly and winter start year. The risk set has 260 spell days and 83 terminations: the two spells whose last day is the last day of February are right-censored. ERA5 box means of 1000- and 850-hPa fields and MSLP exclude grid points above 1000 m. q is controlled across the 39 causal predictors. The four same-day centred R values (±7-day window) use information from after day k; they are shown as non-causal diagnostics and are excluded from the false-discovery-rate correction. Intervals are 95% winter-block bootstrap intervals and p-values two-sided plus-one bootstrap p-values, 2(min(n≤0, n≥0) + 1)/(B + 1), from B = 10,000 resamples.

## Table S4. Termination hazard model: cloud, humidity and radiation before and during the terminating night

ERA5 hourly fields from the ARCO archive, Bangladesh box. “Before terminating night”: means over 00–11 UTC of day k (06–17 LT), 00 UTC (06 LT) dawn values, and day-to-day changes of the daytime means; these can carry precursor information. “Terminating night”: means over 12–23 UTC (18–05 LT), which overlap the night that decides whether the spell continues; these are concurrent with the outcome. Radiation accumulations (J m⁻²) were converted to mean fluxes by dividing by the accumulation time (3600 s per hourly field). q is controlled separately within each window; the global correction across all 61 causal predictors is given in the main text. Intervals are 95% winter-block bootstrap intervals and p-values two-sided plus-one bootstrap p-values, 2(min(n≤0, n≥0) + 1)/(B + 1), from B = 10,000 resamples.

## Table S8. Leakage-free comparisons of persistent and short cold-night spells, with minimum detectable differences

Event-window means of 14 drivers in three windows of identical event status, related to duration in two ways: persistent minus short difference (units as in Table S8; SD for the Siberian High, NAM and RRWP measures; fraction for Ural blocking; K day⁻¹ for 850-hPa advection; degrees and m s⁻¹ for jet latitude and speed), and Spearman correlation with duration across all 85 spells. Rossby-wave measures enter only in causal form (R lagged by 7 days; trailing 3-day envelope). q: false discovery rate within each window and statistic. Minimum detectable ρ: the smallest absolute correlation detectable with 80% power at a two-sided 5% level (2.80 × bootstrap standard error; nominal, single comparison).
